newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka rupee up, depreciation exercise at end.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka rupee up, depreciation exercise at end.

text.p: The Sri Lanka rupee closed stronger on Tuesday as banks sold dollars on speculation that the 1996 depreciation of the local unit had ended.
The rupee closed at 56.52 to the dollar after opening at 56.60, The rupee closed at 56.63 on Tuesday.
"The fundamental reason which made banks sell dollars when call rates rose, was the belief that the dollar has risen about as high as it will go this year," said a Hatton National Bank dealer.
Call rates hit a high of 21 percent due to seasonal pressure on money, he said.
Some dealers, however, say the rise in call money was not entirely warranted given the extent of liquidity available in the market.
Wednesday's Treasury Bill auctions which were about 2.5 times over-subscribed, is an indication of the amount of liquidity, they said.
Bids received at the auction amounted to 9.7 billion rupees, with only 3.8 rupees accepted.
